question: Which Mughal emperor is known for designing a series of inlays behind his throne in the court at Delhi that depicted the legendary Greek god Orpheus playing the lute?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shah Jahan** was the Mughal emperor known for his love of art and architecture.
 
• He designed a series of inlays behind his throne in the court at Delhi.
 
• These inlays depicted the legendary Greek god Orpheus playing the lute.
 
• The throne was placed in the Diwan-i-Am (Hall of Public Audience) in the Red Fort in Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shah Jahan's Reign**

 
 
• Shah Jahan ruled from 1628 to 1658 and is best known for commissioning the Taj Mahal.
 
• His reign is considered the golden age of Mughal architecture.
 
• He also built the Peacock Throne, another iconic piece of Mughal artistry.
 
 
 
• **Orpheus in Art**
 
 
• Orpheus is a figure from Greek mythology known for his musical abilities.
 
• He is often depicted playing the lyre or lute, charming animals, and even inanimate objects.
 
• His story has been a popular subject in Western art for centuries.
 
 
 
• **Diwan-i-Am**
 
 
• It is the Hall of Public Audience in the Red Fort of Delhi, where the emperor would meet his subjects.
 
• It features a raised platform for the emperor's throne.
 
• The hall is richly decorated with intricate carvings and inlays.
